images.prompt: Photorealistic macro photograph of a handcrafted miniature tabletop diorama. A brushed graphite clipboard about the size of a tablet lies at a slight angle on a pale neutral tabletop, holding a thin packet of four ivory paper forms with crisp edges and faint lines of blank fields. Its chamfered clip is closed on the packet, and a single acid-lime tab marks the signature page as the only step left. To the right, a frosted acrylic document tray waits empty. Behind the clipboard, a small ivory card box of blank tabbed dividers stands upright. A slim graphite pen lies parallel to the clipboard. Along the top edge of the packet, a second loose form is just starting to slip in beneath the clip. Fibre grain and pencil dust show on the paper. Everything is calm. Wide 16:9 landscape frame. The hero object sits slightly left of centre on the lower third, with the related objects extending to the right so the workflow reads left to right. Clean, generous negative space above. Shot as a real physical model, not a 3D render. Materials are limited and tactile: heavyweight ivory cotton paper and card with visible fibres, soft folds and slightly deckled edges; matte, bead-blasted graphite metal with fine machining lines, chamfered edges and tiny hex fasteners; frosted acrylic with milky edges and a soft internal glow; sandblasted frosted glass. Surfaces carry believable imperfections: fine dust, paper grain, hairline creases, light scuffs on metal. Every object has convincing miniature scale and weight and rests firmly on its surface. Colour palette is restrained and nearly monochrome: white #FFFFFF, warm ivory, pale neutral #F3F5F2, soft grey-green #DCE1DA, muted graphite #626A64 and deep graphite #191D1B. Acid lime #D0F344 appears only on the lime element named in the scene, as the single signal colour, with olive #718D0B on its shadowed sides. Nothing else is lime or saturated; no red, orange or blue accents. Lighting: one large soft key light from the upper left at about 45 degrees, like diffused north-window daylight, with a gentle white bounce fill from the right; soft grounded contact shadows fall to the lower right. Camera: 100mm macro lens at f/4, eye level with the tabletop, three-quarter view. The hero object is tack sharp and the background melts into smooth, creamy blur on a seamless pale neutral sweep. Mood: calm, precise, orderly and quietly premium, like high-end editorial product photography. Strictly no people, figures, faces, hands or silhouettes. No readable text, letters, numbers, clock digits, logos, signage or user-interface graphics anywhere. No holograms, floating screens, robots with faces, dense cable tangles, carnival or circus elements, cartoon or plastic CGI look, oversaturated colour, lens flare or heavy vignette.

The forms have multiplied into a tall, leaning tower of ivory sheets many times the clipboard's height, pinned only at the base by the straining clip, which is bent open. The tower bows to the right, and its upper third is frozen mid-collapse, sheets peeling off in slow fans and gliding toward the frosted tray, which is already overfilled and cracked at one corner. The acid-lime signature tab is visible deep in the lower stack, squeezed flat. The divider box has been knocked over, spilling blank tabs. The graphite pen is skidding away. Dust and paper fibres swirl in the air, and the lean points straight back to the clip. Wide 16:9 landscape frame, same layout and angle as the calm version of this scene. Nothing else is lime or saturated; no red, orange or blue accents. A rolling desert of ivory paper dunes, each dune built from layered weathered forms with wind-frayed edges, stretches toward a shimmering horizon under a hard low sun. Half buried on a dune crest is the building-sized graphite clipboard, its clip snapped and jutting upward like a broken arch, pale fibre drifting over it. The frosted acrylic tray lies cracked in a hollow, filled with paper sediment. Ripples of loose sheets cross the slopes. In the midground, a slim graphite crawler with a long boom carries an acid-lime binding clamp, which is gathering one small, neat packet of forms from the dune slope and pressing it square and tight between its jaws, leaving a flattened clean trail behind. Wide 16:9 panoramic frame. The main ruin anchors the left or centre foreground, terrain rolls back to a distant horizon on the upper third, and the lime recovery rig sits in the right midground. Surfaces carry believable imperfections: fine dust, paper grain, hairline creases, light scuffs on metal. Every object has convincing miniature scale and weight and rests firmly on its surface. Acid lime #D0F344 appears only on the lime element named in the scene, as the single signal colour, with olive #718D0B on its shadowed sides. Nothing else is lime or saturated; no red, orange or blue accents.
